subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped dry-run security contract should OpenClaw expose for agent tool execution across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, and hooks?
rationale: This would become a user-trusted no-side-effects boundary, and current source shows multiple execution paths where a process-global or partial interception design could be unsafe.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify CLI and runtime semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, and embedded paths.

options.title: Defer to broader workflow modes
options.body: Keep this blocked until Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode design chooses the shared vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Keep only scoped command-level dry-runs if maintainers decide a global preview boundary is too easy to misunderstand as a sandbox guarantee.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify CLI and runtime semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, and embedded paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal for the agent tool adapter and adjacent hook/security semantics.
